On The 27th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 44052 of 2025
 Prem Sunder Mandal
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri M.K. Rajak - Advocate for applicant.
Shri Manoj Chaturvedi - Advocate for objector.
Shri Praveen Namdeo - Government Advocate.

Order 
Case diary is not available.

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.322/2024 registered at Police Station - Maihar, District - Satna for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376(2) of the IPC and Section 5 and 6 of POCSO Act.

Applicant is in custody since 22.08.2025.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 02/04/2024 the complainant (mother of prosecutix) went to Civil Hospital at 11:00 a.m. for her treatment, she left her two daughters in the house, when she return back to her house at 02:30 p.m. she did not find small daughter and when she asked from her elder daughter, then she told her that she went to Delha Turning for treatment, but she did not return back.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49748 2 MCRC-44052-2025 Then the complainant inquired her small daughter from doctor at Delha Turning, then the doctor told her the she did not came here.

After some time, she informed to her mother by telephonic message that she is going to Damoh, she was talking with one Prem Sunder i.e. present applicant who is working at Ultratech Cement Factory and the present applicant allured the prosecutrix/victim, on that the aforesaid report of the complainant has been registered under the aforesaid offences.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
The statement of prosecutrix has been recorded and she is the consenting party.
Trial will take time to be concluded, hence, the applicant be released on bail.
4. Prosecutrix is present in the Court with Shri Manoj Chaturvedi, learned counsel for complainant and she has no objection, if the applicant is enlarged on bail.
5. Learned counsel for State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that no case of bail is made out.
Hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

6. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties and perused the case diary.
7.
Looking to the factual aspect of the case coupled with the fact that trial will take time to be concluded, this Court deems it fit to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Hence, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:49748 3 MCRC-44052-2025 furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during pendency of trial.

9. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
10.
Accordingly, Misc. Criminal Case stands disposed of. C.c. as per rules.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE DPS Prem Sunder Mandal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132693133/
